questions.subject: Cardiology
questions.lead_in: A 64-year-old man with a history of hypertension presents with exertional chest pressure relieved by rest. ECG shows no acute changes. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
questions.plain_name: A 64-year-old man with hypertension presents with exertional chest pressure...
questions.plain_explanation: Stable angina with a non-diagnostic resting ECG is best evaluated with exercise stress testing to risk-stratify before considering invasive angiography. Immediate angiography is reserved for high-risk or unstable presentations.

questions.subject: Nephrology
questions.lead_in: A 52-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes has a urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio of 320 mg/g. Which medication class best slows progression of her kidney disease?
questions.plain_name: A 52-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and albuminuria...
questions.plain_explanation: ACE inhibitors and ARBs reduce intraglomerular pressure and albuminuria, slowing diabetic kidney disease progression. They are first-line in diabetics with albuminuria.

questions.subject: Infectious Disease
questions.lead_in: Which organism is the most common cause of community-acquired bacterial pneumonia in adults?
questions.plain_name: Most common cause of community-acquired bacterial pneumonia...
questions.plain_explanation: Streptococcus pneumoniae remains the most common bacterial cause of community-acquired pneumonia in adults.

questions.subject: Endocrinology
questions.lead_in: A patient presents with fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, and an elevated TSH with low free T4. What is the diagnosis?
questions.plain_name: Fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, elevated TSH, low free T4...
questions.plain_explanation: Elevated TSH with low free T4 indicates primary hypothyroidism — the thyroid gland fails and the pituitary compensates with increased TSH.

questions.subject: Hematology/Oncology
questions.lead_in: A 30-year-old woman has microcytic anemia with low ferritin and low transferrin saturation. What is the most likely cause?
questions.plain_name: Microcytic anemia with low ferritin and low transferrin saturation...
questions.plain_explanation: Low ferritin is the most specific indicator of iron deficiency. Combined with low transferrin saturation and microcytosis, iron deficiency anemia is the diagnosis.

questions.subject: NGN Case Study
questions.lead_in: For each potential intervention, click to specify whether it is Indicated or Contraindicated for a client in diabetic ketoacidosis.
questions.plain_explanation: DKA management centers on IV fluids, an insulin infusion, and careful potassium monitoring/replacement. Oral agents are inappropriate in acute DKA, and potassium should not be withheld since insulin drives K+ intracellularly.
